# CI

`workflows/ci.yml` runs one job per kind of failure, so a red check names what broke (a check under about 30 seconds is a named step of a related job instead, since each job is billed by the whole minute): `lint-frontend` (ESLint, Prettier, `npm run lint:rules`, `tsc` for `client/` and `e2e/`, and `scripts/check-versions.sh` and `scripts/check-no-skipped-tests.sh`), `unit-backend` (Spotless, then Surefire and the JaCoCo gate, no Node), `unit-frontend` (the contract test, then Vitest and its coverage thresholds), `build` (the bundled jar, built with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8080`), `integration` (the `*IT` classes against the built frontend), `e2e` (Playwright against the jar), `docker` (builds the production `Dockerfile` image, runs it with `--memory=512m` in the `prod` profile against a Postgres 17 container, calls the API, checks the game is in Postgres and fails if the container logged an `ERROR` or `OutOfMemoryError`) and `data` (`scripts/check-processed-data.sh`).

- `changes` picks the jobs a PR needs from its changed files (a change to `.github/` or `scripts/`, and every run that is not a PR, runs all of them). Each job is gated by the `changes` output of its own name, so a new job needs an output, a filter and the gate. `test` is the aggregate: it needs all of them and fails unless each succeeded or was skipped as not needed, and it is the one required status check on `main`, so keep its id and name.
- Each Java job caches `~/.m2` with `actions/cache` under its own key (`m2-<job>-…`). Never use `setup-java`'s `cache: maven`: it shares one key, the first job to finish saves only its own dependencies, and the rest download from Maven Central until it answers 429.
- CI does not run on a push to `main`: branch protection makes a PR up to date with `main` before it merges, so its last run tested the merge. Pull requests cancel superseded runs; every other run has its own concurrency group. A draft PR runs nothing (`changes` and `test` are skipped) until it is marked ready for review (`converted_to_draft` is a trigger only so that going back to draft cancels the run in progress).
- `build` hands the jar and `client/out` to `integration` and `e2e` through `actions/cache` (key `ci-build-<run id>`), never as artifacts, and every report `upload-artifact` sets `retention-days: 3`: artifact storage counts against the account quota (the default 90 days filled it and every upload step failed), the cache does not.
- CI also runs every Monday morning and on demand (`workflow_dispatch`), with no push: it finds breakage that arrives without a commit (the runner image, the floating Docker base tags Render also builds from, Playwright's system packages).
- `smoke-production.yml` is the only workflow that touches the network (it calls the deployed services, on demand and daily) and never runs on a PR. Nothing run on a PR may reach the internet, and no test may hit the network.
